Module 1.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>LPP Graphical Convex Feasible Polygon</text><text x='110' y='75' fill='#10b981' font-size='14'>Maximize Z = c₁x₁ + c₂x₂ subject to Ax ≤ b, x ≥ 0</text></svg>
Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP504 Module 1
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Standard LPP Form: $\max Z = \mathbf{c}^T \mathbf{x}$ subject to $\mathbf{Ax} = \mathbf{b}, \mathbf{x} \ge 0$
  • Simplex Optimality Condition: All net evaluation coefficients $C_j - Z_j \le 0$ for maximization problem.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Slack, Surplus, Artificial Variables: Slack adds to '$\le$' constraints; Surplus subtracts from '$\ge$' constraints with Big-M/Two-Phase artificial variables.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Optimal solution always lies at an extreme corner point of the convex feasible region.

Module 2.title: Duality & Sensitivity Analysis
Module 2.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Primal-Dual Mathematical Equivalence</text><text x='100' y='75' fill='#fcd34d' font-size='14'>Max Z_primal = Min W_dual (Strong Duality Theorem)</text></svg>
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP504 Module 2
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Primal-Dual Relationship: Primal has $m$ constraints & $n$ variables $\iff$ Dual has $n$ constraints & $m$ variables.
  • Shadow Price: Rate of change of optimal objective value with respect to marginal increase in resource availability ($y_i^* = \partial Z^* / \partial b_i$).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Complementary Slackness: $x_j (C_j - Z_j) = 0$ and $y_i (b_i - \mathbf{A}_i \mathbf{x}) = 0$.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Dual of dual is primal.

Module 3.title: Transportation & Assignment Models
Module 3.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Vogel's Approximation (VAM) & MODI Optimality</text><text x='110' y='75' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='14'>u_i + v_j = c_ij (Allocated cells) • Δ_ij = c_ij - (u_i + v_j)</text></svg>
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP504 Module 3
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Initial Basic Feasible Solution (IBFS): Vogel's Approximation Method (VAM) yields closest to optimal by penalizing differences between two lowest cell costs.
  • MODI (u-v) Optimality Test: Calculate $u_i + v_j = c_{ij}$ for allocated cells; optimal if $\Delta_{ij} = c_{ij} - (u_i + v_j) \ge 0$ for all empty cells.
  • Hungarian Method (Assignment): Subtract row minimum -> Subtract column minimum -> Cover zeros with minimum lines -> Augment uncovered elements.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Degeneracy in Transportation: Occurs when allocated cells $< m + n - 1$; resolved by adding infinitesimal quantity $\epsilon$ to least cost independent cell.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Hungarian assignment requires square matrix $n \times n$; add dummy row/column with zero costs if unbalanced.

Module 4.title: Project Management: CPM & PERT
Module 4.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>PERT Probabilistic Expected Activity Time</text><text x='120' y='75' fill='#f59e0b' font-size='15'>t_e = (t_o + 4·t_m + t_p) / 6 • σ = (t_p - t_o) / 6</text></svg>
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP504 Module 4
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • PERT Expected Time ($t_e$): $t_e = \frac{t_o + 4t_m + t_p}{6}$ (Optimistic, Most likely, Pessimistic)
  • Activity Variance ($\sigma^2$): $\sigma^2 = \left(\frac{t_p - t_o}{6}\right)^2$
  • Total Float ($TF$): $TF = LS - ES = LF - EF$ (Activities on critical path have zero total float)
  • Project Completion Probability: $Z = \frac{T_s - T_e}{\sigma_{\text{project}}}$, where $\sigma_{\text{project}} = \sqrt{\sum_{\text{critical}} \sigma_i^2}$
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • CPM vs PERT: CPM is deterministic (construction, known times); PERT is probabilistic (R&D, 3 time estimates).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Critical path is the longest sequence of activities connecting start to finish; delay on critical path delays entire project.

Module 5.title: Queuing Theory: M/M/1 Model Dynamics
Module 5.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>(M/M/1):(∞/FCFS) Single Server Queuing Model</text><text x='90' y='75' fill='#10b981' font-size='14'>Traffic Intensity ρ = λ / μ < 1 • L_s = ρ / (1 - ρ) = λ / (μ - λ)</text></svg>
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP504 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Traffic Intensity / Utilization ($\rho$): $\rho = \frac{\lambda}{\mu} < 1$ (where $\lambda$ is arrival rate, $\mu$ is service rate)
  • Expected Customers in System ($L_s$): $L_s = \frac{\lambda}{\mu - \lambda} = \frac{\rho}{1 - \rho}$
  • Expected Customers in Queue ($L_q$): $L_q = \frac{\lambda^2}{\mu(\mu - \lambda)} = L_s - \rho$
  • Little's Law: $L_s = \lambda W_s$, $L_q = \lambda W_q$ (Waiting time in system $W_s = W_q + \frac{1}{\mu}$)
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Poisson & Exponential Distribution: Arrivals follow Poisson distribution with mean $\lambda$; Service times follow Exponential distribution with mean $1/\mu$.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • If $\rho \ge 1$, the queue grows infinitely without reaching steady state.
